submission.rationale: The action contract states task.checkpoint requires expectedRevision and a stale expectedRevision fails with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. The planning evidence (revision 3, frontier=beta-concurrent) may no longer match the current Task state, and the intended consequence is explicitly conditional on "if the newer Task state still supports that semantic transition." Without re-observing the current revision/frontier, I cannot safely know whether the checkpoint will commit or conflict. Acting now risks hitting a stale expectedRevision (producing a false/conflicting consequence), while HOLD would abandon useful progress. The contract even provides a resume path ("after resume a semantically still-applicable checkpoint may be rebased"), implying re-observation is the correct gate before committing or rebasing. I therefore reobserve to obtain the current revision and checkpoint state before choosing among checkpoint-now, rebase-and-act, or hold.
